headline: The American Medical Association has published a framework of four questions for judging AI agents that carry out tasks in patient care.
score_reason: Voluntary guidance from a major medical body; no binding force, score unchanged.
importance_line: Doctors and hospitals get a shared checklist on what AI agents may do and who is accountable, but it is guidance, not law, and many agents are already in use.
summary: Healthcare Dive reports that the American Medical Association, the largest US physicians' group, released a governance framework built on four questions, including what an AI agent is allowed to do and who is responsible for it. It arrives as a survey cited by the outlet found about 28% of 250 US healthcare leaders already use agentic AI, tools that finish multi-step tasks on their own, and 72% said such tools are sometimes adopted without IT approval.
notes: Only some of the four questions appear in the retrieved text.
